title: Statistical Inference as Severe Testing (Excursion 1, Tour I)
summary: Mayo introduces severity as a criterion for assessing how much evidence a test result supplies for a specific claim. The author-posted excerpt develops the criterion and distinguishes it from judging a method solely by its long-run performance.
established: Section 1.1 argues that agreement supplies evidence for a claim to the extent that the test would probably have revealed a specified flaw if present.
Severity attaches to the claim and the particular result. A probe can be sensitive to a large departure and insensitive to a smaller one.
